# .github

## CI (`workflows/ci.yml`)

Runs `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high` → lint → knip → knip:production → format check → CSP hash check → pkg:build → typecheck → apps:build → `pnpm test` → SonarCloud, and Playwright plus a report-only ZAP baseline against the local API in a separate `e2e` job. Every workflow is pinned to `ubuntu-26.04`; nothing uses `ubuntu-latest`. Its kernel 7.0 trips MongoDB's refusal to start on kernels 6.19+ ([SERVER-121912](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-121912)), so the Testcontainers Mongo (`apps/server/test/integration/setup/global-setup.ts`) and the e2e compose Mongo set `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=1`; drop it from either and that suite fails on CI only. The Postman collection (`postman/collections/Trellify.postman_collection.json`) and the k6 load tests remain the manual and performance checks; Lighthouse audits of production are run locally.

There is deliberately **no Lighthouse workflow** — see `.claude/rules/lighthouse.md` before adding one.

## Deploy (`workflows/build-k8s-images.yml`)

Runs on `workflow_run` of `CI`, only when CI **passed** on a push to `main` (a failed run sends a Telegram notice instead and deploys nothing). It checks out `workflow_run.head_sha`, never `github.sha`, which in a `workflow_run` event is whatever `main` points to by then. It skips the build when nothing outside `infra/**` and `*.md` changed since the commit the overlay currently pins, which replaces the `paths-ignore` that `workflow_run` cannot use. Otherwise it builds the image to `ghcr.io/baoduong254/trellify-server:sha-<short>` and `deploy-client` runs `wrangler deploy` from `apps/client` (`wrangler.jsonc`, secrets `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`/`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`), then a second job runs `kustomize edit set image` in `infra/apps/trellify/overlays/prod` and pushes a `chore(deploy): ... [skip ci]` commit. The `[skip ci]` marker stops CI from running on that commit, and so stops it from triggering another build — don't remove it. `latest` is published but never deployed; the overlay pins the sha tag plus the image digest (`kustomize edit set image ...:<tag>@<digest>`), and the runtime pulls by digest, so an overwritten tag on GHCR cannot change what runs. The bump fails rather than pin a tag alone.

A nightly `schedule` run Trivy-scans the pinned server image and, only on a fixable HIGH/CRITICAL CVE in an OS (Alpine) package, rebuilds the **deployed** commit (never `main` HEAD, which may not have passed CI) as `sha-<short>-<YYYYMMDDHHMM>`; `workflow_dispatch` gets the same suffix. The gate passes `--pkg-types os` on purpose: a rebuild cannot fix a JS or Node CVE (that needs a lockfile or base-image bump through Renovate), so counting them would rebuild and roll the pods every night for nothing. Never give a rebuild the plain `sha-<short>` tag: it would overwrite an immutable tag and the bump would be a no-op, so nothing rolls. `APK_UPGRADE_DATE` (UTC date) is a build arg on the server Dockerfile so the `apk upgrade` layer cannot be restored from the GHA cache forever. The scheduled bump skips itself if the overlay moved during the rebuild, so it never rolls back a newer deploy. Each pushed digest also gets BuildKit SBOM/provenance, a Trivy scan and a cosign keyless signature; a fixable CRITICAL CVE fails `build-and-push`, so `bump-manifest` never runs and nothing deploys.

Releases are automated by release-please. GitHub secret scanning (push protection + alerts) is the server-side secret layer; there is no gitleaks step in CI.
